text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and U.S. President Bill Clinton discussed an acceptable formula for resuming Syrian-Israeli negotiations with U.S. help. Mubarak told a news conference that there was no justification for wasting the progress achieved in previous negotiations between Syria and Israel and that Israel must reconsider settlement activity in Jerusalem and must not commit new violations.
- Mubarak also met Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Secretary of Defence William Cohen. Today he will meet members of Congress.
- The government is preparing new legislation to regulate the stock exchange, Economy Minister Nawal el-Tatawi said.
- Cabinet Affairs Minister Talaat Hammad said the government would cover 20 percent of the costs of investment in the South Valley Development project.

- Mubarak told the Christian Science Monitor that the U.S. veto of a U.N. resolution on Jerusalem was regrettable. He said it gave the Israelis a signal that they can go on building settlements, although most countries say it offends Arabs.
- Pharaonic statue found by chance in Zagazig.
- Education Minister Hussein Kamel Bahaeddin said no building would be allowed in school playgrounds.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the World Bank had asked to take part in the South Valley Development project, denying a report that the World Bank had refused to finance it.
- Businessmen denied that during Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's visit to Egypt it was agreed to set up an Israeli-Egyptian businessmen's council.

- Housing Minister Mohamed Ibrahim Soleiman said shops in new towns would be allocated to central Cairo shopkeepers who lose their shops as a result of a Constitutional Court ruling that their shop leases are not inheritable.
